transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-07 15:00 PT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Priya (Bluehaven Head of ML Ops), Carlos (Platform Eng), Aisha (Product)

Summary section (auto-gen - may be rough):
Redwood: quarter over quarter usage up ~2.4x, tail latencies spik- spikes during checkout personalization, cost concentrated in long-chat sessions and embeddings for search. Discussed Dedicated reserved capacity for Black Friday and fallback policies to hosted. Security & audit docs requested.

Topics discussed:
- Traffic pattern: daily peak 6–9pm EST, sustained bursts during promo emails
- Costs: embeddings and rerank are biggest token consumers, cache hit-rate low for product recents
- Reliability: 2 incidents in last 90 days, transient KV cache misses during autoscaler events
- Roadmap: plan to migrate checkout personalization to dedicated pool for 72-hr Black Friday runway
- Compliance: SSO, SAML, SOC2, KMS/HSM, VPC peering questions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie: okay all right hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Sophie from Redwood, uh with Daniel and Maya. quick agenda — usage/costs, reliability, and the plan for the holiday peak.
[00:22] Priya: hi thanks, yeah we saw token growth this quarter uh pretty big, mostly from the recommendation embeddings and the live chat personalization. we wanted to align on cost levers and what dedicated would look like for a short runway.
[00:35] Daniel: cool, and just to set expectations, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated GPU pools, you can pin model versions, and we can do canaries + auto-fallback to hosted if capacity saturates. there's tradeoffs on commit cost vs per-token savings.
[00:52] Carlos: quick clarifying q — we currently use Hosted with an app-level cache, but the prefix / KV cache hit rate is only about 28%, so embeddings are recomputing a lot. would dedicated change cache behavior?
[01:08] Daniel: good question. dedicated doesn't change semantic cache behavior by default, but moving inference closer to the KV store (same VPC) and enabling Redwood prefix caching at the pool level typically raises hit-rate. we can also recommend a short TTL for product recency to bump hits.
[01:28] Aisha: and latency—checkout paths need sub-150ms 95th percentile, right now we're seeing 180–220ms during peak, which is a problem.
[01:38] Sophie: got it. for 95th p95 under 150ms we usually recommend reserved capacity with a burst buffer and pre-warmed KV caches. also model size and quantization profile matters; smaller quantized variants sometimes hit the latency SLO better.
[01:56] Priya: can you explain the fallback behavior? if we hit the dedicated pool limit do we automatically spill to hosted? what's the latency penalty?
[02:05] Daniel: yes, policy driven — we can route by latency or cost. if dedicated is full we either queue or route to hosted variant. hosted will sometimes be slightly higher latency due to multi-tenant scheduling but we can pick a compatible model family to preserve quality. average penalty we've measured is ~30–80ms depending on model.
[02:25] Carlos: there were two incidents in sept where autoscaler took 6–8 minutes to scale and we saw KV miss storms — any mitigation?
[02:35] Daniel: we saw logs — autoscaler cool-down config and aggressive downscaling was the culprit. recommended steps: lengthen cooldown, add standby capacity/scale-up buffer for promo windows, and enable proactive batching thresholds to reduce scale churn.
[02:52] Priya: ok makes sense. on security, our infosec wants SOC2 attestations, audit logs retention for a year, SSO via SAML, and KMS support — are those in place?
[03:08] Maya: yes we can share our SOC2 report and audit log retention options, we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Private deployments and we also offer KMS integration for Dedicated with limited key types. SSO and RBAC are fully supported.
[03:25] Aisha: would Private (VPC/on-prem) be overkill for us? we mostly need residency and tighter controls for some data but not full air-gap.
[03:34] Sophie: sounds like Dedicated with VPC peering might hit the sweet spot — you get isolation and lower latency without full private control plane. Private deployment is recommended if you have regulatory requirements or need full control over keys.
[03:48] Priya: pricing — can you send the committed tier numbers? we need to compare cost to current hosted burn.
[03:55] Sophie: sure we'll send a few commit options; also include a short-run Dedicated window pricing for the 72hr Black Friday runway — that's often cheaper than bursting hosted at scale.
[04:07] Carlos: about benchmarking — we want to run a checkout flow benchmark with a 60k RPS-ish token pattern for 6 hours during non-business hours, can Redwood run that?
[04:19] Daniel: yes, we'll provide a runbook and we'll need a 2-hour coordination window to set up KV warmers and pre-warm caches. propose Nov 18–20 for the window.
[04:30] Priya: perfect. any suggestions for lowering embedding costs? we use embeddings for search and personalization heavily.
[04:37] Daniel: two levers — first, pre-compute and store static embeddings for catalog items and only recompute for new items; second, use quantized smaller embedding models for approximate search, and hybrid rerank: use cheap vector search + small reranker for top-k. also consider caching top-k per user cohort.
[04:57] Sophie: there's also Redwood Optimize suggestions we'll share — batching windows, recommended quantization profiles, and per-route cost breakdown to identify hot routes.
[05:07] Aisha: what's the contract SLA for Dedicated? uptime and latency SLOs?
[05:12] Maya: Dedicated includes an SLA-backed uptime target and latency commitments per model tier — we'll share the SLA sheet. there are escalation paths and runbook access for on-call during events.
[05:25] Priya: ok next steps — Sophie to send pricing and targeted commit plans, Daniel to send benchmark runbook, Maya to share SOC2 and KMS docs, Priya to confirm test dates.
[05:36] Sophie: awesome, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark window and share docs in the next 48 hours. thanks everyone.
[05:45] Carlos: thanks all, that was helpful.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional word errors (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache"), some overlapping speech masked, names sometimes abbreviated.
